correctness.rationale: The Perron spectral-radius formula is exact. Write C=1+A+B, where A is binomial and B counts indirect peripheral vertices. The directed two-step path count Z has exact mean ns(s-1)p^2(1-p), with E|B-Z| bounded by open paths of length at least three and duplicate two-step paths. Sharing-edge covariance analysis gives Var Z=O(s+\(s^{3/2}\)/\(\sqrt n\)) at p=c/rho. Hence B/s converges in probability to \(c^{2}\) for \(s\to\infty\) and \(s=o(n)\); E B=O(s) also covers bounded s. The CLT for A and Slutsky prove the finite cubic-scale Gaussian shift and its above-scale divergence. The standalone exhaustive exact-rational checker passed 203236 assertions; asymptotic proof is independent of finite checks.

value.rationale: An irregular host family has an exact spectral scale at which direct hub neighbors fluctuate normally; growing peripheral cliques create an indirect, geometry-driven population. Showing exactly when this population is negligible, produces a finite normal-mean shift, or overwhelms direct-neighbor fluctuations is a natural finite-graph percolation resolution with a sharp and non-arbitrary \(n^{1/3}\) boundary. The theorem does not overclaim a new giant-component transition.
